messages.text: Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in Lesotho changed by +5.8% per year (95% CI: +3.3% to +8.1%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is +10.2% relative to the previous 12 months.

messages.why: classification of 78 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10
messages.text: Of 78 ADM2 units, 55 show significant growth, 19 are stagnating and 1 are declining. Light remains concentrated: Maseru District accounts for 41% of national light.
Across ADM2 units, light per capita converges: the least-lit units are catching up.

The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is −0.33 in levels (95% CI: −3.41 to 2.75, R² = 0.00, 12 years) and −0.19 in growth rates (CI: −1.82 to 1.44). Out of sample, light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of −0.96 (mean absolute error: 3.6 percentage points of growth).

messages.why: trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability
messages.text: The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of -14.2% (12/2020), return to the pre-shock level after 12 months.

messages.why: sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 0.03 to 0.04 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection
messages.text: The Gini coefficient of light per capita (ADM2) is 0.53 in 2025 (significant decrease since 2014). About 0.03 million people live in inhabited areas with no detectable light (39% of the inhabited population).

messages.why: precision 92% and recall 22% against the reference list
messages.text: 12 industrial clusters detected from concordant satellite signals: 3 heavy industry, 2 business parks & logistics, 2 oil & gas sites and 5 isolated sites to verify. They emit 16.0% of national light (latest year); their light changes by +1.0% per year. Maseru District has the most industrial activity.

messages.why: correlation of 0.87 with international tourist arrivals (WDI) (6 years)
messages.text: 11 of 77 units show a net summer light excess of at least 10%: Ratau (Maseru District), Mafeteng (Mafeteng District), Tayateyaneng (Berea District), Mohale's Hoek (Mohale's Hoek District). The median net excess reaches +21% in the most touristic zone. The season index (base 100 = 2019) falls to 224 in 2020 and stands at 87 in 2025.

messages.why: rank correlation of 0.25 with GHSL built-up growth (68 units)
messages.text: The lit area changes by +10.9% per year, against +1.2% for population. Of 78 ADM2 units: 65 show electrified urbanisation, 1 balanced growth, 1 unlit growth. Between 2014 and 2025, 789 km² became lit, of which 130 km² in already inhabited areas (≈ 7k newly lit inhabitants). Largest expansion: Kanana (Berea District), Qiloane (Maseru District), Seate (Mokhotlong District).

recommendations: Use night-time lights as a leading and subnational indicator, as a complement to — never a replacement for — the national accounts.
Do not disseminate light-based GDP estimates: the NTL–GDP relationship is not established with sufficient confidence over this period.
Cross-check the map of populations “in the dark” against grid-connection registers: the average gap with the World Bank access rate is +11 percentage points.
Document breaks detected without an associated event (sensor change, outage, local event) before any economic interpretation.
Have the 5 isolated sites checked on high-resolution imagery and complete the official register of industrial zones used as the validation reference.
Monitor the light of industrial clusters monthly as a leading indicator of industrial output, and compare it with the industrial production index where one exists.
Publish the tourist season index right after the summer (VIIRS data are available within weeks), ahead of hotel-night statistics, and recalibrate it on them every year.
Cross newly lit areas with urban plans and grid-connection registers to tell planned expansion, informal settlements and rural electrification apart.
Prioritise infrastructure (power grid, services) where population grows faster than the lit area: Semonkong (Maseru District).
Update the dashboard every quarter (monthly VIIRS series) and every year (annual VNL composites).

limits.title: What lights measure
limits.text: Upward radiance emitted around 01:30: agriculture, daytime trade, poorly lit services and the rural informal economy are poorly captured.

limits.title: Saturation and blooming
limits.text: DMSP saturates in city centres (DN 63) and “blooms” beyond lit areas; VIIRS is much better, but blooming still inflates the lit area of cities.

limits.title: Gas flares and isolated sites
limits.text: The automatic mask may remove isolated mines, ports or power plants, and miss small flares; candidates are exported for verification.

limits.title: Clouds, seasons, moon
limits.text: Cloudy months are only partially observed; STL removes average seasonality but not an abnormal season (snow, late monsoon).

limits.title: Product breaks
limits.text: DMSP and VIIRS are not directly comparable: the harmonised long series (Li et al., 2020) is a modelled product, to be read for trends only.

limits.title: NTL–GDP elasticity
limits.text: Estimated on 10 to 30 annual observations: wide intervals, possible instability, a non-causal relationship that varies with the level of development.

limits.title: Access to electricity
limits.text: “Inhabited without light” ≠ “not connected”: a connected household with low consumption is invisible; the indicator depends strongly on the radiance threshold and the population data.

limits.title: Administrative boundaries
limits.text: geoBoundaries/GAUL may differ from official boundaries; small ADM2 units are sensitive to light spilling over from neighbouring units.

limits.title: Industrial zones
limits.text: Detection relies on thresholds: a power plant, a port or a large shopping centre can meet the signals; a dimly lit factory without visible emissions is missed. Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) are coarser than VIIRS: NO₂/SO₂/heat signals describe a neighbourhood, not a building.

limits.title: Summer tourism
limits.text: The summer excess captures any rise in summer light (second homes, diaspora visits, festivals, construction), not only tourism; at high latitudes, very short summer nights reduce VIIRS observations. Ramadan changes night-time activity: the summers concerned are flagged.

limits.title: Urbanisation
limits.text: The lit area depends on the detection threshold and on light blooming around cities; a connected but dimly lit neighbourhood stays invisible. Population (GHSL/WorldPop) is modelled from censuses: its growth is not an independent observation, and years between two epochs are interpolated.
